Nausea book jacket, New Classics series

Alvin Lustig draws a knot of loose calligraphic strokes twice, once in black and once in white, slightly offset on an olive jacket.

Source
Wikimedia Commons: Nausea.jpg (photograph by Karen Horton)
Creator
Alvin Lustig
Made
c. 1952 (Commons caption)
Style
Mid-century modern (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Literary, restless, modern, crafted
Evidence
Inspected, in the scratchpad only, the 1280 px Commons rendition of Karen Horton’s photograph of a copy of the jacket (original 2478 × 2859 px). The copy shows edge wear at the top. No museum copy was checked.
Reviewed
28 September 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

The Commons caption credits the jacket design to Alvin Lustig for the New Classics series published by New Directions, c. 1952. The photograph is by Karen Horton and is licensed CC BY 2.0. Commons.

Lustig lived from 1915 to 1955. Wikidata. Sartre’s novel was first published in French in 1938; Lloyd Alexander translated it into English. Wikipedia: Nausea (novel)).

Observed

  • The jacket is flat olive-brown.
  • “nausea” at upper left and “sartre” at lower left are lowercase italic serif in off-white.
  • The center holds an abstract knot of strokes: straight bars, hooks, arcs, and a V shape. Each stroke is drawn twice, once in black and once in off-white, with the two copies offset by a few millimetres.
  • “lustig” is signed in small black script at the right of the knot.
  • There is no frame or rule; the strokes float on the olive ground.

Why it belongs

The offset black and white copies read like a two-color print out of register, the same effect the style uses as overprint.

The lowercase italic title and the loose marks show how Lustig paired quiet book type with expressive, hand-made imagery.

Borrow

Draw a mark twice in two colors and offset the copies slightly to suggest a print out of register.

Set titles in lowercase italic serif and let the image do the loud work.
